territorial_scope.description: Applies to the FAA and to air traffic facilities across the United States national airspace system.

summary.short: Directs the FAA Administrator to review AI and machine learning applications for airport efficiency and safety, research AI-enabled controller training, and direct use of big data analytics and machine learning in Part 107 waiver processing. Applies to the FAA; reports to Congress are due within one year of enactment.
summary.long: Sections 1024, 1028 and 908 direct the FAA Administrator; they impose no duties on private parties and set no thresholds or penalties. Section 1024 requires a review of current and planned AI and machine learning technologies for airport efficiency and safety, including jet bridges, airport service vehicles, aircraft taxi and air traffic control, and a report to Congress within one year of enactment. Section 1028 requires, subject to appropriations, a research program on AI, machine learning and other technologies for air traffic controller training, with collaboration with labor organizations and a report within one year. Section 908 directs a performance- and risk-based review of Part 107 drone waivers under 14 CFR 107.200, including a standardized application format, use of prior waiver data and big data analytics and machine learning, consideration of applicant property-access control, online publication of waivers, streamlined approval of similar applications and expedited modification review.
